source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: The layered-witness convention reflects the manuscript-attestation reality: Aramaic DSS fragments are FRAGMENTARY (preserve only portions of chs 1-36); Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus preserves chs 1-32 substantially complete; Ge'ez is the only complete witness but the most distant in time and language from the Aramaic original. Per-verse selection prioritizes the oldest preserved witness; alternate witnesses documented where they differ materially or provide cross-collation value.

verses.text: אסתכלו בכל עבדא די בשמיא איך לא שניו אורחתהון ובמאוריא די בשמיא איך כלהון דנחין ושקעין כל חד וחד באדנה ולא עברין על פקודיהון
verses.translit: ʾistakkalū bě-kol ʿăbādāʾ dī bě-šĕmayyāʾ ʾēk lāʾ šanniyū ʾorḥāthōn ū-bě-māʾōrayyāʾ dī bě-šĕmayyāʾ ʾēk kullhōn dānĕḥīn wĕ-šāqʿīn kol ḥad wĕ-ḥad bě-ʿiddāneh wĕ-lāʾ ʿābrīn ʿal puqdēhōn
verses.text_greek: Κατανοήσατε πάντα τὰ ἔργα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, πῶς οὐκ ἠλλοίωσαν τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν, καὶ τοὺς φωστῆρας τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὡς πάντες ἀνατέλλουσι καὶ δύνουσιν τεταγμένως ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ καιρῷ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῖς ἑορταῖς αὐτῶν φαίνονται, καὶ οὐ παραβαίνουσιν τὴν ἰδίαν τάξιν.
verses.text_geez: ኅሥሡ፡ ኵሎ፡ ምግባረ፡ ዘውስተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ከመ፡ ኢሤነዉ፡ ፍናዊሆሙ፡ ወብርሃናተ፡ ዘውስተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ከመ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ይሠርቁ፡ ወይዐርቡ፡ ሥሙራነ፡ አሐዱ፡ አሐዱ፡ በበጊዜሁ፡ ወኢይትዐደዉ፡ እምሥርዐቶሙ፡
verses.notes: Contemplate-the-heavens framing — the natural-order argument. The verb אסתכלו 'observe attentively' opens a wisdom-trope: nature obeys its order; humanity does not. This anticipates the Astronomical Book (chs 72-82). Cross-corpus: cf. Wis 13:1-5 (natural-theology argument); cf. Sir 43; cf. Ps 19:1-6.

verses.text_greek: ἴδετε τὴν γῆν καὶ κατανοήσατε ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπὸ πρώτων ἕως ἐσχάτων, ὅτι οὐδὲν ἔργον θεοῦ παραβαίνει ἀπὸ τῆς τάξεως αὐτοῦ· πάντα οὕτως φαίνεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: idete tēn gēn kai katanoēsate apo tōn ergōn tōn en autē apo prōtōn heōs eschatōn, hoti ouden ergon theou parabainei apo tēs taxeōs autou; panta houtōs phainetai hymin.
verses.text_aramaic: חזו בארעא ואסתכלו בעבדא די בה מן קדמיא עד אחרניא
verses.text_geez: ርእዩ፡ ምድረ፡ ወኅሥሡ፡ እምነ፡ ምግባር፡ ዘውስቴታ፡ እምቀዳምያን፡ እስከ፡ ደኃርያን፡ ከመ፡ አልቦ፡ ምግባረ፡ ዘእግዚአብሔር፡ ዘይትዐደው፡ እምሥርዐቱ፡ ኵሉ፡ ከመዝ፡ ይትዐየን፡ ለክሙ፡
verses.notes: Earth-order parallels heaven-order; no work of God transgresses its appointed order. The principle θεοῦ παραβαίνει 'God's [work] transgresses' contrasts with human transgression (developed in vv. 4-5).

verses.text_greek: ἴδετε τὴν θερείαν καὶ τὸν χειμῶνα ὁποίως πλήρης ὁ κόσμος πᾶς ὑδάτων· καὶ νεφέλη καὶ δρόσος καὶ ὑετὸς ἐπ' αὐτῇ ἀναπαύεται.
verses.translit: idete tēn thereian kai ton cheimōna hopoiōs plērēs ho kosmos pas hydatōn; kai nephelē kai drosos kai hyetos ep' autē anapauetai.
verses.text_geez: ርእዩ፡ ሐጋየ፡ ወክረምተ፡ እፎ፡ ዓለም፡ ኵሉ፡ ምሉእ፡ ማይ፡ ወደመና፡ ወጠል፡ ወዝናም፡ ላዕሌሁ፡ የዐርፍ፡
verses.notes: Summer/winter contrast — second observation in the natural-order sequence. The Greek θερείαν (summer) + χειμῶνα (winter) is the standard Hellenistic seasonal-dichotomy. Aramaic of 2:3 is not preserved.
